decisions.reason: Requiring full through-hole access to the ESP32-S3 pins does not change any existing functional GPIO assignment.
The breakout and generic-platform decision does not change the standalone USB power source, capacity, activation condition, or powered scope.
The reference to possible future projects with buttons is descriptive of reuse and does not modify the current panel controls, connectors, or mappings.
Full ESP32-S3 pin breakout access does not alter the monitored rails, monitor IC, channel count, or current-measurement topology.
The source does not change the current SK6812 supply voltage, direct data drive, LED model, or power-control behavior.
The breakout decision does not modify the I2C series-resistor value, population policy, purpose, or topology.

Although the retained breakout constrains routing, the source does not change the board dimensions, ESP32 edge placement, connector arrangement, orientation, or other recorded mechanical-layout attributes; the smaller pitch is only proposed as a question.
The source does not change either power source, the Schottky OR-ing method, or source-selection behavior.

The candidate records the JST and USB-C connector inventory and architecture; retaining a separate ESP32 through-hole breakout does not change those recorded connector counts or destinations, and no header pitch is finalized in this message.
The requirement for local decoupling capacitors remains unchanged by the ESP32 breakout decision.
The source does not affect the buzzer type, prototype part, or accepted substitute.
The full-pin breakout decision does not alter the switched rail, MOSFET topology, switching side, or transistor pair.
